question:
A researcher is studying how electrical activity propagates across the heart. In order to do this, he decides to measure the rate at which an action potential moves within various groups of cardiac muscle tissue. In particular, he isolates fibers from areas of the heart with the following characteristics:

A) Dysfunction leads to fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
B) Dysfunction leads to increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
C) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex
D) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on electrocardiogram

Which of the following is the proper order of these tissues from fastest action potential propagation to slowest action potential propagation.?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: D -> tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on electrocardiogram -> slowest action potential propagation -> 80% CHAIN: C -> tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex -> slower action potential propagation than D -> 75% CHAIN: B -> increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat -> slower action potential propagation than C -> 70% CHAIN: A -> fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat -> slowest action potential propagation -> 80%
analysis: The proper order of tissues from fastest action potential propagation to slowest action potential propagation is D > C > A > B. Tissues with dysfunction leading to tachycardia typically have faster action potential propagation compared to tissues with dysfunction leading to fixed or increasing PR intervals.
